coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Avalon at Mission Bay III
record.summary: Avalon at Mission Bay III, an AvalonBay apartment community whose grand opening AvalonBay announced on June 18, 2009.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- official DataSF Assessor parcel boundary (blklot 8705006), ~6093 sq m, not a hand trace or plan estimate. 353-383 King St and 260 units per the DataSF Assessor roll (parcel 8705006; AvalonBay's release also gives 260 units, and DataSF Parcels gives the address range 200-298 Berry St); grand opening June 18, 2009 per AvalonBay's own investor-relations press release. This is the whole site/land parcel, not just the building's rooftop -- it includes any courtyard, landscaping or parking within the lot line. Correction 2026-09-29: this is a single Assessor parcel; no per-unit condominium lots map to 8705006 in DataSF's Assessor parcel data (the earlier condo-mapping statement was wrong), and why this record is not tied directly to that Assessor lot is not established here.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Parcels -- Active and Retired (blklot 8705006, real cadastral land-parcel boundary)

milestones.text: Avalon at Mission Bay Phase III (addressed as 240 Berry St in contemporary coverage; same project as 353 King St) under way: SocketSite's post 'Starts Its Ascent' notes a construction webcam and flyers advertising 260 apartments, a 17-story tower and an 8-story mid-rise, coming mid-2009
Avalon at Mission Bay III (353 King St) grand opening

changes.text: The map notes said the parcel's many per-unit condo lots share its footprint; the DataSF parcel data has only the parcel itself, so the claim was replaced with a correction. The 353-383 King St address and 260 units now cite the DataSF Assessor roll, the 'three phases along King St' note was reduced to what AvalonBay's release says, the 2009 grand-opening milestone links the release, and the 2007 milestone links the SocketSite post and no longer says the building topped out.
changes.source: AvalonBay Communities, 2009-06-18 (https://investors.avalonbay.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/333/avalonbay-celebrates-grand-opening-of-avalon-at-mission-bay-iii-a-community-committed-to-sustainable-living); DataSF Assessor Historical Secured Property Tax Rolls, parcel 8705006 (https://data.sf.gov/resource/wv5m-vpq2.json?parcel_number=8705006); DataSF Parcels (https://data.sfgov.org/Geographic-Locations-and-Boundaries/Parcels-Active-and-Retired/acdm-wktn); SocketSite, 2007-12 (https://socketsite.com/archives/2007/12/avalon_at_mission_bay_phase_iii_240_berry_starts_to_ris.html)

Its summary is limited to what its cited source confirmed when re-read that day; fuller details recorded elsewhere in Pier & Point's data (developer, architect, unit count, year built) were left out where that source didn't state them. Not yet researched: no milestones, costs or facts.
